claims.text: Adding 1–2 vol% Y2O3 nanoparticles to a refractory high-entropy alloy will enhance its radiation tolerance.
Adding 1–2 vol% Y2O3 nanoparticles will maintain the alloy's mechanical integrity.
Mechanical alloying followed by hot isostatic pressing can produce the proposed baseline refractory high-entropy alloy.
Incorporating Y2O3 during mechanical alloying will achieve a uniform nanoscale oxide distribution.
The proposed effect is expected under high-dose neutron irradiation at approximately 400°C for about 1000 hours under static or low-strain-rate loading.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles will be distributed both along grain boundaries and within grains.
Distributed Y2O3 nanoparticles serve as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
The nanoscale oxide particles trap radiation-induced point defects and defect clusters.
Trapping point defects and clusters reduces the accumulation of irradiation-induced dislocation loops.
Reduced defect and dislocation-loop accumulation mitigates radiation-induced embrittlement and swelling.
The defect-sink mechanism preserves microstructural integrity and mechanical properties under high radiation flux.
Relative to the unmodified alloy, the Y2O3-containing alloy will have a lower post-irradiation defect density.
Relative to the unmodified alloy, the Y2O3-containing alloy will exhibit less irradiation-induced swelling.
Relative to the unmodified alloy, the Y2O3-containing alloy will retain tensile strength and hardness better after irradiation.
The unmodified baseline will accumulate higher defect densities during irradiation, leading to degraded mechanical properties.
The anticipated benefits are bounded to approximately 1–2 vol% Y2O3 and the specified irradiation conditions.
Significantly higher oxide contents or different irradiation temperatures or doses may eliminate the benefits or impair mechanical performance.
The proposed defect-sink mechanism is well supported in other oxide-dispersion-strengthened alloys.
The magnitude of radiation-tolerance and mechanical-property improvement in refractory high-entropy alloys remains unquantified.
